claims.text: V1.3 1DD is a blend, not a single-instrument record: SSM/I then SSMIS (DMSP F13, F17; RSS Tb CDRs from NCEI) give rain frequency; CPC 3-hourly geostationary IR (GOES, Meteosat, GMS/MTSAT) with NOAA AVHRR leo-IR fill-in is the main input in 40°N-S; TOVS (to 2002) then Aqua AIRS give high latitudes; GPCP Monthly V2.3 (which holds the GPCC gauges) sets the monthly totals.

evidence.passage: Specifically, 1. SSMI, then SSMIS (0.5°x0.5° by orbit, GPROF algorithm) provides fractional occurrence of precipitation, and 2. GPCP monthly analysis Version 2.3 (2.5°x2.5°) provides monthly accumulation of precipitation to algorithms applied to 3. Geosynchronous-orbit IR (geo-IR) Tb histograms (1°x1° grid in the band 40°N-40°S, 3- hourly), 4. Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer (AVHRR) low-orbit IR (leo-IR) GPI (same time/space grid as geo-IR), and 5. TIROS Operational Vertical Sounder, then Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (TOVS, AIRS; 1°x1° on daily nodes, Susskind algorithm). Although microwave precipitation estimates and gauge analyses are not explicitly used due to sampling limitations, the calibration of the Daily to the GPCP Monthly Version 2.3 ensures that they do have a strong influence on the overall scaling.

Table 1: Inputs to GPCP Daily Analysis | Name Data GPCP time Data Notes | type period source | RSS SSMI Tb Tb 1996 to NCEI F13: 1996 to 2008 | CDR 2008 | RSS SSMIS Tb Tb 2009 to NCEI Replaces SSM/I Tb; data only from F17 | CDR present | GPCP Monthly Precip 1996 to NCEI | Analysis V2.3 present | TOVS Precip 1996 to GPCP/GSFC | 2002 | AIRS V6 Precip 2003 to GSFC DISC Replaces TOVS | present | IR 3 hourly Tb 1996 to CPC | files present

The GPCP daily product blends data from polar-orbit passive microwave satellites (SSMI, SSMIS), polar orbit IR sounders (TOVS, AIRS), geostationary infrared satellites (GOES, MeteoSat, GMS, MTSat) and the GPCP monthly analysis. … For the period October 1996 - February 1999, the TOVS estimates are based on two NOAA satellites. Beginning in March 1999, the TOVS estimates are based on a single NOAA satellite. … The Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS) aboard the NASA Aqua polar-orbiting satellite is the source of precipitation estimates to follow-on after TOVS (in 2005). … Gaps in geosynchronous coverage (most notably over the Indian Ocean before METEOSAT-5 began imaging there in June 1998) are filled with IR data from the NOAA-series polar-orbiting meteorological satellites.

claims.text: V1.3 is made fully by algorithm: the Threshold-Matched Precipitation Index (a GPI-type IR method whose Tb threshold matches SSM/I rain frequency and whose rain rate makes the month sum to GPCP Monthly) in 40°N-S, rescaled TOVS/AIRS outside, smoothed across 40-50°; gauges enter only through the monthly calibration; updated two months after each month ends.

evidence.passage: The differences between the IR and TOVS (AIRS) datasets required that the Daily be formulated in two parts, with smoothing over the latitude band 40° to 50° in each hemisphere to help transition across the data boundary. … In the latitude band 40°N-S the Threshold-Matched Precipitation Index (TMPI) produces approximate instantaneous precipitation from the geo-IR Tb with fill-in by rescaled leo-IR GPI. It is a GPI-type algorithm with locally calibrated Tb threshold and rainrate. … Then a single rainrate for "raining" geo-IR pixels is computed for each grid box that makes the full month of TMPI sum to the local GPCP Monthly value. … for each month in each hemisphere the local number of TOVS (AIRS) rain days was reduced by the ratio of the total number of TMPI and TOVS (AIRS) rain days at latitude 40°. The remaining non-zero daily rain amounts are rescaled to start at zero and sum over the month to the local GPCP Monthly value.

claims.text: The V3 daily computes no new precipitation estimates: it averages IMERG to 0.5° daily, thresholds it at 0.24 mm/d, histogram-calibrates TOVS/AIRS to IMERG, feathers the 55° seam, then ratio-adjusts the days to the Monthly (ratios capped 0.2-4); updates were roughly quarterly.
